newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Embratel plan Dec launch of Brasilsat B3 satellite.
newsitem.headline: Embratel plan Dec launch of Brasilsat B3 satellite.

text.p: Brazil's long-distance telecoms monopoly Embratel said it plans to launch in December its Brasilsat B3 satellite, which will operate on the C band frequency.
A company spokesman said the satellite will provide regional and national coverage and will begin commercial operation in March 1998. No launch date was set.
He said he could not confirm how many transponders, which receive and transmits signals aimed at the satellite the B3 will have, but local news agency InvestNews said it will have 28 transponders.
"Our other satellites have 24 but this one just may have 28," the spokesman said.
He also said Brazil and Argentina will sign a contract in July to establish procedures for Buenos Aires to use Brasilsat B3 and Brazil to use Argentina's Nahuelsat.
The communications ministries of both countries in March signed an agreement allowing the combined use of one another's satellites, he said.
Embratel, a unit of Brazilian telecommunications holding Telebras, is slated to be sold in early 1998 as part of the overall privatization of the federal telecoms system.
